Narrative:
On March 5, 2025, a 2024 GMC Sierra was traveling north on US-395  in Deer Park, Washington with Super Cruise engaged and active. According to OnStar audio recordings, a vehicle traveling west on a cross-road to US-395 entered the intersection and the GMC  Sierra struck the vehicle on the driver's side.  According to telematics, crash data indicates a frontal impact that deployed the driver front airbag and front seat belt pretensioners of the GMC Sierra. The driver was buckled at the time of the crash. The GMC Sierra was traveling approximately 63 mph and Super Cruise was Engaged and Active at the time of the crash.
Update:  On November 28, 2025, GM received remote EDR event data that indicated Super Cruise transitioned to "Disabled/Not Ready" 1.1 seconds prior to the crash following a driver takeover via brake pedal application.

Narrative: On October 25, 2025, a GMC Hummer EV was traveling westbound on I-10 in Gramercy, Louisiana, with Super Cruise engaged and active.  Crash data indicated a frontal impact occurred that deployed the airbags and front seat belt pretensioners.  The driver was wearing a seat belt at the time of the crash.  According to OnStar recordings, the driver reported hitting a vehicle parked in the middle of the highway with no lights on and that the struck vehicle left the roadway and landed upside down in the adjacent woods. Telematics data indicates the system changed to "Degraded Escalation" 4 seconds prior to the crash due to a loss of communication with the front camera, then changed to "Disable/Not Ready" 3 seconds prior to the crash due to a driver take over. Weather condition at the time of the crash is unknown.
